question: Explain when an arrangement is treated as an 'impermissible avoidance arrangement' under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in the Income-tax Act, 1961, and the consequences that follow.
sources: Income-tax Act, 1961, Chapter X-A (sections 95 to 102), sections 90(2A) and 144BA

points.label: Main purpose test
points.description: The main purpose of the arrangement must be to obtain a tax benefit; an arrangement is presumed to have that main purpose if the main purpose of any step in it, or part of it, is to obtain a tax benefit, even if the whole arrangement has another main purpose.

points.label: The tainted elements
points.description: In addition, the arrangement must create rights or obligations not normally created between persons dealing at arm's length, result in misuse or abuse of the Act, lack commercial substance, or be carried out in a way not normally used for genuine purposes.

points.label: Lack of commercial substance
points.description: An arrangement lacks commercial substance where, for example, its substance differs significantly from its form, it involves round trip financing or an accommodating party, its elements offset each other, or it disguises the value, location or ownership of funds, or locates an asset or transaction mainly to obtain a tax benefit.

points.label: Consequences
points.description: The tax consequences are determined as if the arrangement had not been entered into, for example by disregarding or recharacterising steps, ignoring an accommodating party, reallocating income or expenses, looking through a corporate structure, treating equity as debt or the reverse, or denying a treaty benefit.

points.label: Procedure and threshold
points.description: The Assessing Officer refers the case to the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner, and if needed to the Approving Panel, before invoking GAAR; it applies only where the tax benefit from the arrangement in the year exceeds the threshold prescribed in the Rules, and it overrides treaty benefits.
points.basis: Income-tax Act, 1961, section 144BA and section 90(2A); Income-tax Rules, 1962, rule 10U
